title: Commitment Curation & Skill‑Shelf Playbook for Cycle Slicing
creator: Lina Rodriguez
description: Problem: Teams repeatedly overcommit mid-cycle and lack a standardized mechanism to defer scope without jeopardizing OKR outcomes. This ticket delivers a lightweight playbook and templates to help PMs and managers curate commitments, create a rotating "skill-shelf" for specialist work, and apply a clear, repeatable scope‑deferral cadence.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook document published to Confluence with versioned template and decision matrix
PM + Eng leads sign-off (explicit Slack thread approval)
Two pilot teams complete a trial cycle using the playbook with recorded outcomes
Operational templates added: commitment worksheet, contingency buffer ledger, skill-shelf roster
decisions: Adopt a single-buffer accounting model (2.5 engineer-weeks per 6-week cycle) rather than percentage-of-velocity to simplify rollups
Skill-shelf roster will be maintained centrally in the PM workspace and updated weekly by leads
Scope deferral requires documented trade-off and a nominated owner to pick up work in the following cycle

decisions_rationale: Single-buffer accounting chosen to minimize bookkeeping overhead and give small projects predictable runway
Centralized skill-shelf reduces duplicate recruiting-style requests to specialists and clarifies pick-up responsibility
Requiring a nominated owner for deferred work prevents orphaned backlog items and improves accountability
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Skill-shelf becomes a black hole for low-priority tasks. Mitigation: weekly triage and SLA for pickup (max 2 cycles)
Risk: Teams pad velocity to game buffer. Mitigation: sampling audit and explicit sign-off by manager on commitment worksheet
Risk: Cross-team dependencies hidden. Mitigation: dependency tags and mandatory dependency owner field on deferral form
